toast.$description: Transient, self-dismissing feedback — 'toast' is the industry-standard name for exactly this pattern (Radix Toast, shadcn's toast, Sonner, Material's Snackbar, Ant Design's `message` are all the same idea with different positions/stacking); 'notification' in most libraries means the richer, longer-lived card with a title, body and actions, which this deliberately is NOT (deferred until a real surface needs one). One line: role icon + text, floating top-center over the page, auto-dismissing on a timer. Three roles per the driving request — success / danger / warning — with icon colors from the status.* semantic group, whose own $description reserves it for exactly this use ('badges, alerts, form validation'); first consumer of that group. The shell reuses Popover's floating recipe (surface.default + border.default + shadow.sm + radius.default): it floats, so it gets a shadow (allowed — floating-UI family), and carries a crisp hairline edge. Implementation is native-first like every overlay in this system: popover='manual' + showPopover() — free top-layer, and 'manual' opts OUT of light-dismiss (a toast dismisses itself on a timer, not on outside clicks) — with a @starting-style entry transition. Built 2026-07-24 for the Student Message Center prototype's archive confirmation. Deferred, not forgotten: close (×) button, inline action link, title+body notification variant, a stacking manager for multiple simultaneous toasts.

offsetTop.$description: Distance from the top edge of the viewport to the toast — top-center placement per the driving request.

role.$description: Which status icon shows and its color — the toast surface itself stays neutral (white + hairline + shadow) at every role, per the flat aesthetic; only the icon carries the meaning. Icons: check_circle (success) / error (danger) / warning (warning), all from the shared Material set.
